title: Repertoire and instrumentation of the country brass band
summary: The bands played marches, one-steps and quick steps; a band of 13-14 had tenors, altos, E-flat clarinets, one valve trombone, four cornets, tuba and two drums.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Would there be much difference between the Dairange band and the Magnolia band and say, Tom Albert's band? What would the difference be?
Well, I didn't find no difference because they all was playing the same type of music. What kind of music was that?
One step, quick step, they were playing all different kinds of music. They didn't fool no, like that, like simple opera music, they didn't fool with that on the time. No, none of the classical.

But they had to like them, six-eight, them boys, just play that stuff, you know. Take twelve of them men and play as much as a big simple opera. How many were in a brass band? Well, it was, it was, it was 13 or 14, 14 men, I think. You see, at the time, they used the pecan. Yeah. Used the first tenor, solo alto, first alto, and used the, what am I saying? The tenor. Is that like the baritone horn? Yeah, like a baritone horn, I understand, a tenor. Is it upright? Upright, yeah, a tenor, I understand, upright. It may look a baritone, but it's not as big as a baritone horn. Yeah. You see, that's the time when them bands didn't have all them, like they got now, tenor sax, they used a baritone, just used them with baritone and clanny, you see? E flat clanny, they used all that kind of stuff. And E flat clanny. E flat clanny, yeah. E flat, yeah. E flat, and short one, E flat clanny.
How many trombones did they have in a band?
Well, they didn't use them with one trombone at a time. One trombone. One trombone. That was a val trombone, yeah. Val trombone. Used a tuba?
Yeah. Is it the upright horn?
No, upright, upright. Upright. Yeah, upright.
Two drums. Snare drum and big drum. Bass drum.
